title: Meet your Command Centre
summary: A quick, friendly tour of the first screen you see: key numbers, what needs attention, search and quick actions.

steps.voice: Hey there! Welcome to [[A]] [[T]] [[A]] [[M]] Flow. This is your Command Centre, mission control for every order.
Up top are your key numbers. Every tile is a live count of what is happening right now.
Tap a tile, like overdue orders, and Flow jumps straight to that list.
Boom! Just the overdue orders, ready to sort, filter and search.
Down here is what needs attention now, with the reason and the next step for each one.
Hunting for something? Hit slash, or control K, and search orders, stock, purchase orders, bins, anything.
Quick actions holds your one-click jobs, like syncing stock or raising a purchase order.
And the production pulse shows what is moving, what is stuck, and what might run late.
And that is the Command Centre! Pop back to the How-to videos page for more. See you next time!

title: Raise and approve a purchase order
summary: Turn orders that are waiting on stock into supplier purchase orders, then approve them.

steps.voice: Time to buy some stock! Head to Purchasing. That is where all your supplier orders live.
Hit the blue Create [[P]] [[O]] button.
Flow lists the customer orders still waiting on stock, already grouped by supplier.
Tick what you want, check where each delivery goes, and raise it. Easy.
Your new [[P]] [[O]] opens as a draft. Nothing goes to the supplier until somebody approves it.
Approving commits you to buying these goods, so Flow shows you exactly who is allowed to.
As set up here, managers can approve up to five hundred pounds. Anything bigger needs an admin.
Press Approve [[P]] [[O]] and it is ready to email. Flow always lets you review the email first.
That is it! Raised, approved, and on its way. Nice work.

title: Generate and print labels
summary: Make order and bin labels, preview exactly what will print, and print them with a record of who did it.

steps.voice: Labels keep your warehouse running smoothly. This list shows everything waiting to be printed.
Need new ones? Hit Generate labels.
Pick a label type, then tick the orders you want. Done in seconds.
Do not worry about doing it twice. Unchanged labels are left alone, and changed ones are flagged for a reprint.
Click a label to see exactly what will print: the order, the customer, the due date and a scannable [[Q]] [[R]] code.
Choose a hundred by one fifty millimetre label, or [[A]] four paper.
Hit Print, and Flow records who printed it and when, so a reprint always has a reason.
And that is labels! Stick them on and keep things moving.

title: Find any order, fast
summary: Ready-made views, filters and search on All Orders, then open any order.

steps.voice: Every open order lives on All Orders, with a reason for where it is and what happens next.
These chips are ready-made views: overdue, at risk, blocked by stock, ready for dispatch and more.
Tap Overdue and the list narrows to just those orders, with how many days late each one is.
Or search by order number, customer, purchase order, producer or bin.
Like a filter you built? Save it as a view, or export the list to a spreadsheet.
Click any row to open the order and see everything about it. That is the next video.

title: Why the system says this
summary: Open an order and see why Flow decided what it did, plus the tabs for everything else about it.

steps.voice: Open an order and the top shows its due date, priority, units, value and how much stock is secured.
Here is the clever part. Flow explains why it made each decision, in plain words.
Stock allocation shows a score, with bars for what helped, like due date and VIP, and what pulled it down.
Across the top are tabs for lines and stock, artwork, purchasing, warehouse, exceptions and history.
Lines and stock lists every item, how many are needed, and exactly how many are short.
Ready to send the work out? Send to a decorator opens a consignment with this order's lines ready.

title: Stock and shortage advice
summary: Find what is short, then let Flow suggest what to do about it.

steps.voice: The Stock page lists every item: what is available, what is reserved, and what is on the way.
Use the chips to jump to low stock, out of stock, or items short for orders.
Short for orders shows only the items that customers are waiting on.
Open an item and Flow advises you: wait, substitute, reorder, split, or tell the customer.
It lists the orders that need the item, and the purchase orders already on the way.
And it recommends how many to buy, so raising a purchase order takes seconds.

title: Review supplier emails
summary: Where supplier emails wait for approval, and why nothing is ever sent by surprise.

steps.voice: Flow drafts supplier emails for you, but it never sends one until a person approves it.
Drafts wait here, under Emails. Each one shows what it is about and who it is for.
This one chases a stock shortage on a purchase order, and is waiting for review.
Approve and send stays greyed out until the supplier has an email address on file.
Not right? Cancel it, and nothing is sent.
Orders running late? Draft chases for late purchase orders writes the emails for you to check.

title: Book a delivery in
summary: Receive a supplier delivery against its purchase order and let Flow flag shortages and damage.

steps.voice: When a delivery arrives, open Goods in and pick the purchase order it is for.
Each one shows the supplier, how many units are outstanding, and when they were due.
For each line, enter how many arrived good, damaged, or the wrong item.
If part of the order is still on its way, tick More coming.
Add your name and the supplier's delivery note number, then paste links to any photos, and notes.
Check the summary, press Book in delivery, and stock updates. Shortages or damage raise a supplier issue.

title: Artwork, proofs and job packs
summary: See whether every order's artwork is ready, how proofs work, and what a job pack is.

steps.voice: Artwork and Job Packs shows, for every decorated order, whether the artwork is ready to go.
Chips pick out orders with missing artwork, unapproved files, or file problems.
Tabs cover customer proofs, file versions, job packs, and artwork arriving from Google Drive.
Open an order to see its artwork area by area, with every file version and its approval status.
Customer proofs record what was sent and what the customer said. An approval only counts for the artwork they saw.
A job pack bundles the lines, quantities and approved artwork for the decorator.

title: Quality checks and rework
summary: Record a quality check, see what gets checked, and follow rework through to a fix.

steps.voice: Quality shows orders waiting for a check, with rework jobs and replacements alongside.
Tabs split the work into things to check, rework jobs, past checks, and the checklist.
Press Record check, choose the order, and mark each point on the checklist as pass or fail.
Add notes and photo links if you need them, then record the result.
The checklist lists what gets checked. These starter items are placeholders until your real standards are confirmed.
If something fails, rework tracks the fix, whether that is a redo or a replacement.

title: Dispatch and courier labels
summary: Pack an order, make the courier labels, see what blocks it, and hand parcels over.

steps.voice: Dispatch is where finished orders go out: pack, print the courier label, add tracking, and hand over.
The tiles count what is ready to pack, blocked, packed and waiting, and with the courier.
Open an order that is ready, enter the parcels and weights, and press Pack and make labels.
If something is wrong, Flow says exactly what is stopping it, like artwork changing after approval.
Packed parcels wait for the courier. Hand over scan records the hand-over, one label at a time.
Marking an order shipped is still done in DecoNetwork.

title: Exceptions: raise, assign, resolve
summary: Work through everything that is wrong or unknown: see it, take it, resolve it, or raise your own.

steps.voice: Exceptions lists everything wrong or unknown, each with an owner and a next step.
The tiles show how many are open, critical, overdue, blocking work, or without an owner.
Needs a person lists the urgent ones, and you can filter by who should handle them.
Open one to see what is wrong, the recommended action, and the impact on the customer.
Then take it, add a note, resolve it, mark it not a real issue, or write it off.
Spotted something Flow missed? Raise an issue, say what is wrong, and give it an owner.

title: The holding pen
summary: Why an order is held back for a data problem, what it cannot do while held, and how it gets out.

steps.voice: When an order has a data problem, it goes into the holding pen so nothing can go wrong with it.
While it is held, it is left out of production planning and cannot be dispatched or completed.
The list says what is wrong: no delivery address, no due date, or no shipping method.
Chips pick out overdue orders, ones with no owner, and orders that are not in Flow yet.
Open a case to see why it is held, what to fix, and its history.
Fix the problem in DecoNetwork and the order leaves the pen by itself after the next sync. This screen is read-only.
